notes.title: Major Upgrade to Unity 6 and Unity 7
notes.content:
[b]Greeting Agents![/b]

It’s time for another major update! Some of you may have heard about our previous plans to migrate to Unreal Engine 5. After some heavy technical evaluation and unity getting there act together, we’ve made the decision to stick with Unity due to the significant challenges in porting over our unreleased mechanics and features to UE5. But don’t worry—there’s still plenty of exciting stuff on the horizon!

We are full steam ahead on [b][i]Anti-Extinction[/i][/b], now on Unity 6, with Unity 7 support coming soon to the alpha branch in our playtest version.



[h1]What’s New Since We Last Spoke?
[/h1]
A lot has happened, so let’s dive in:

- [i][b]Unity Issues? Solved[/b]![/i] We’ve overcome several roadblocks we faced with Unity, thank goodness.  
- [b]Demo Delays[/b]: Unfortunately, the release of our demo is delayed due to financial constraints and ongoing efforts to secure new investors.
- [b]Visual & Performance Upgrades:[/b] We’ve revamped our lighting and VFX engines to support [b]HDRP[/b]. We chose HDRP to deliver the visual fidelity we envisioned, which URP couldn’t achieve without significantly more time and resources.  
- [b]Nanite for Unity? Yes, it’s happening! [/b]We’re closely monitoring a third-party company called NanoTech, who are working on bringing Nanite to Unity. This will drastically improve the quality and performance of our world-building. We hope to integrate this tech later this year, with potential updates rolling out as we stabilize it for full production.



[h2]Unity's Latest Updates – What This Means for Us
[/h2]
Here are some official, exciting Unity updates that are relevant to our future plans:

- Unity is making [b]Burst [/b]more tightly integrated into the engine, which will improve performance across the board.
- The transition to [b].NET 8/CoreCLR[/b] is well underway, with the Unity Editor and Players now running on .NET 8 CoreCLR, and Mono officially being phased out.  
- The [b]MSBuild support[/b] for building projects is also progressing, making life easier for all of us devs!

For us, this is massive! A lot of the features we’re developing are built on [b].NET 8[/b]—from gameplay mechanics to our innovative [b]passkey tech[/b]. We're eagerly waiting for further announcements, especially at [b]Unite 2024 in Barcelona[/b], happening September 18–20. Fingers crossed!



[h2]Support Us!
[/h2]
We can’t do this without your help. If you’d like to support the development of **Anti-Extinction**, here’s how:

- Consider [b]donating[/b] or becoming a member on [b]Patreon [/b]or [b]Ko-Fi[/b].
- Purchase some of our content on [b]Gumroad[/b].
- Stream our original soundtrack, [b]Furr-Tec[/b], on your favorite music platform—it’s free and helps us out a ton!



From the entire [i][b]Furr-Tec Development Team[/b][/i], we want to thank you for over 3+ years of incredible support. We hope to have more exciting news (and a playable build!) later this year, once we get the final word from Unity.

Stay tuned and keep the faith!

[b]From the Leadership Team
[/b]A message from us, the Furr-Tec leadership team:

[b]Hephaestus Aether (CEO):
[/b]"We’re pushing the boundaries of what we can achieve, and every bit of your support helps us move forward. Thank you for being part of this journey!"

[b]Jyra Foxx (CCO):
[/b]"Our vision for Anti-Extinction has never been clearer. We’re excited to share this adventure with all of you—let's make something incredible together!"

[b]Apollo (CMO):
[/b]"The road ahead may have challenges, but the reward will be a game that stands the test of time. Keep spreading the word and helping us build the community!"

[b]Caesin (President):
[/b]"From day one, this project has been about innovation and heart. With your continued support, we’re making that vision a reality!"

[b]Koda (Secretary):
[/b]"Every comment, share, and message of encouragement fuels our passion. Thank you for keeping us going!"

notes.title: Feedback on moving to Unreal
notes.content:
I hope you're all doing well! I wanted to share some thoughts and get your feedback on a significant decision we're considering for Anti-Extinction. Due to ongoing issues and lack of support from Unity, we're contemplating a gradual transition from Unity to Unreal Engine. Below is a detailed list of the problems we've been facing:

[b]Core Issues[/b]:
[b]Unstable Editor[/b]: Basic features frequently crash the entire editor window.

[b]SRP (Scriptable Render Pipeline) Issues[/b]: Beyond my control and Unity is not addressing them.

[b]PhysX Problems[/b]: The update from 4.3.1.X to higher versions is causing severe issues with the physics system, which is crucial for Anti-Extinction. Check out the discussions here:
[b]Stuttering Issue[/b] (https://issuetracker.unity3d.com/issues/a-1000-times-heavier-gameobject-will-stutter-when-colliding-with-a-lighter-gameobject)

[b]Physics Performance Regression[/b] (https://forum.unity.com/threads/physics-performance-regression-in-unity-2022-3-8-and-onwards.1495442/#post-9675257)

[b]Garbage Editor Reload[/b]: The editor reload process is inefficient and problematic.

[b].NET 8 Delay[/b]: The absence of .NET 8 means ongoing instability and long waits for editor repaint windows.

[b]Cinemachine Issues[/b]: Working around editor issues, particularly with Cinemachine 3, causes memcpy crashes. Cinemachine 2 is stable but crashes upon updating due to a .TSS file issue.

[b]Potential Benefits of Unreal Engine[/b]:
[b]Stability[/b]: Unreal Engine 5.4 offers more stability and robust features, which could save us time and resources in the long run.
[b]Support[/b]: We can apply for Epic MegaGrants, which could provide the funding we desperately need.

[b]Important Milestones[/b]:
Q3 2024 Demo Release: We plan to release a demo of the game based on the story lore in Q3 2024. This demo will be developed in Unity to ensure we meet our timeline and provide you with a taste of what’s to come.

[b]Transition to Unreal Engine[/b]: After the demo release, we will transition to Unreal Engine to finish the work we started with Furr-Tec from 2022 to now. This move aims to enhance stability and leverage Unreal’s robust features for the final game development stages.

[b]Our Commitment to Quality[/b]
As a dev team, we want to ensure the game is as optimized and bug-free as possible for our consumers. This transition is part of our commitment to delivering the best possible experience. We believe Unreal Engine will help us achieve these goals by providing a more stable and powerful development environment.

[b]Your Feedback[/b]
We understand this is a significant shift, and we want to ensure it aligns with the expectations and support of our community. Here’s what we’re considering:
Gradual Transition: Slowly moving parts of the project to Unreal Engine while continuing some development in Unity to maintain progress and stability.
Community Involvement: Keeping you all updated on our progress and involving you in testing and feedback to ensure the transition improves the game's quality.

We value your thoughts and would love to hear your feedback on this potential transition. Do you think this move is the right step for Anti-Extinction? How do you feel about the potential benefits versus the challenges of such a transition?

Please share your thoughts and questions here
